plates.title: T-RECAP multi-signal system architecture
plates.subtitle: Recorded audio, motion and RF inputs share a fixed-point spectral core and two explicit output representations.

nodes.title: Configured input frontend
body: TRF1: I/Q centering, FIR interpolation and real-IF mapping

nodes.title: Shared spectral-processing core
body: sample ring -> analysis window -> FFT -> Hermitian canonicalizer
power threshold -> paired mask -> IFFT -> WOLA
fixed-point arithmetic, frame metadata and held outputs

nodes.title: Output representation
body: TSP1: dense or sparse masked power records
independent queues with explicit counts and backpressure

description: T-RECAP connects three recorded signal classes to one numerical processing design. Audio and individual acceleration axes use signed real-sample preparation. RF recordings retain their unsigned I/Q bytes until the FPGA frontend centers, interpolates and maps them to a real intermediate-frequency stream.

Linux on the DE1-SoC HPS owns the finite transaction. It verifies the fitted profile, writes source words and drains independent reconstructed-sample and spectral queues. The fabric performs the source conversion and shared fixed-point DSP. The laptop interprets outputs using the original sample rate, units and source metadata.

The implementation is selected at build time. TSH2 fits the real-sample application and TRF1 fits the I/Q application. Both instantiate the same spectral core. The frontend box expresses those configurations and is not a runtime selector. Module boundaries, memories and accepted-transfer behavior are expanded in the following nineteen views.

notes.title: Design contract

description: A source contract includes numerical representation, sample rate, valid length and physical meaning. Audio and motion inputs are prepared as signed 12-bit real samples. Motion axes are replayed individually with their scale metadata so output values can be interpreted in acceleration units.

RF uses interleaved unsigned 8-bit I/Q. The FPGA centers both components, interpolates by four and produces a real IF stream. Its core sample rate is four times the input complex sample rate. Consequently the numerical bin index must be interpreted with the appropriate frontend rate and IF mapping.

Profile identity is a build configuration checked before each transaction. Quantization, RF gain and thresholding are separate numerical operations. Result reports retain these settings rather than combining all input preparation error with the effect of the spectral threshold.

notes.title: Design contract
notes.body: The same core sample value can represent audio amplitude, scaled acceleration or real IF. Sample rate and scale are part of the result contract.

description: The core forms 256-sample windows at a 128-sample hop. Analysis produces signed 27-bit values. A normalized forward FFT yields 28-bit complex bins, then the canonicalizer enforces Hermitian symmetry using widened pair arithmetic and one defined rounding operation.

Power is an unsigned 56-bit squared magnitude. THR2 retains equality and protects DC. The paired complex mask feeds a separate inverse transform while a valid-only observation exposes nonnegative-frequency masked power to the exporter. Sparse encoding changes transport and consumer work rather than the fixed transform schedule.

The inverse engine produces signed 36-bit values. Synthesis applies the window, emits mature overlap-add samples and accumulates the current frame. The Y stream preserves reconstruction information. TSP1 preserves power and bin identity but omits phase. Detailed memories and arithmetic are shown in views 9 through 14.

notes.title: Design contract
notes.body: Core coefficients use 15 fractional bits. RF FIR coefficients use 16. Threshold units are squared fixed-point FFT magnitude.

description: The I/Q frontend accepts one packed unsigned pair per input transfer. It converts each byte to a signed 9-bit centered value and retains 21 samples per component. Four interpolation phases share one multiplier and accumulator. The coefficient address is four times the tap index plus the phase.

The phase sequence selects +I, -Q, -I and +Q to form a real IF stream. FIR coefficients have 16 fractional bits. Gain changes the quantizer shift from 16 down to 13 without changing the core interface. A signed 12-bit sample and its clipping flag are registered and held together.

Alignment discards 40 startup outputs and flushes 10 centered-zero pairs, giving exactly four retained real samples per original pair. The finite wrapper records this valid prefix and pads to the admitted core geometry. Views15 and 16 expand the actual arithmetic resource and controller schedule.

description: Y is the reconstructed real signal produced by the IFFT and WOLA path. It supports listening, waveform comparison, motion detection and conversion to downstream file formats. TSP1 contains masked power rather than complex coefficients. It supports spectrum consumers that can use retained-bin indices directly.

Each TSP1 frame has a 48-byte header. Dense encoding includes 129 seven-byte powers and one padding byte for 952 bytes total. Sparse encoding includes K eight-byte index/power entries for 48+8*K bytes. These spectral transport sizes are separate from WAV, FLAC or reconstructed sample storage.

The laptop first validates identities, framing and checksums. Application-specific consumers then compare quality and workload. Dense and sparse representations at the same threshold carry the same masked powers. Comparing them isolates the representation benefit. Comparing with threshold0 measures the information removed by thresholding.

notes.title: Design contract
notes.body: Power-only TSP1 cannot reconstruct phase-bearing waveforms. Y is the waveform reconstruction output.

description: The laptop supplies a recorded source and explicit configuration. The HPS software validates the application magic, ABI, source digest and geometry before touching the transaction data path. This binds each capture to the fitted application and its register contract.

CLEAR removes stale queue and packet ownership. Configuration writes establish threshold and sparse mode, with pair count and gain for TRF1. START begins an epoch. The service interleaves bounded input writes with reads from both output queues so downstream backpressure can clear.

Hardware DONE is a production boundary. The host also drains remaining data and validates final counts, record identities and checksums. Reports distinguish hardware compute counters, transfer duration, laptop decode work and application work. Detailed register fields and FIFO ownership are shown in views17 through 19.

description: Control is distributed across modules. The input scheduler owns sample history and frame admission, the transform engines own their work RAMs, and the exporter owns packet slots. Metadata queues keep threshold and frame id aligned across variable transform and transport latency.

The finite wrapper gates future source samples using exported-frame credit. Therefore only one triggered frame may remain un-emitted even though the exporter physically has four slots. The spectral observation tap remains valid-only. Backpressure is applied upstream at a safe future admission boundary.

A ready/valid stream transfers only on simultaneous valid and ready. Held registers preserve values and identities across stalls. Sticky faults and watchdog expiry terminate a malformed epoch. CLEAR abandons all related ownership together so data from different epochs cannot silently combine.

notes.title: Design contract
notes.body: Storage capacity and admitted concurrency are different quantities. Frame credit, held words and queue occupancy must be read together.

description: The FPGA application sits behind the HPS bridge on the DE1-SoC platform. CLOCK_50 drives the application fabric. Separate fitted images implement the configured source frontends while sharing the same numerical core implementation and output conventions.

Verification evidence is scoped to the design under test. Module and system simulations check arithmetic, handshakes, framing, malformed access and recovery. Published UVM and formal results retain their own source sets, assumptions and coverage. Their existence does not turn every application result into a formal proof.

Fitter reports establish physical implementation properties for a particular image. Board captures establish output behavior for admitted runs. Application measurements establish quality and workload under their stated inputs and timing boundaries. The atlas connects these layers through exact source bindings and module observation points.

notes.title: Design contract
notes.body: This atlas documents the implemented architecture and its evidence boundaries. Rendering these figures runs no RTL or hardware.

plates.title: Frame storage and analysis-window hardware
plates.subtitle: Accepted samples, tagged overlap storage, coefficient reads and frame-owned thresholds have distinct owners.

nodes.title: Frame scheduler
body: Frame 0 covers -128 through 127. Left half is zero.

description: Only accepted input tokens advance the sample index and write the ring. One 256-sample frame is scheduled per 128 accepted samples. Negative conceptual indices in the first frame generate exact zero. Tags detect overwritten or mismatched sample history.

The analysis multiplier extends the unsigned 16-bit window coefficient with a leading zero before signed multiplication. It fits the product to signed 27 bits without a fractional right shift. The held result includes frame id, offset and last so backpressure does not separate sample data from its identity.

A four-entry metadata FIFO associates THR2 with each admitted frame across FFT latency. Reference history is a separate 1,024-entry store used for the 384-sample error alignment. Ring storage depth and metadata capacity do not imply that all entries can be simultaneously in flight as independent frames.

notes.title: Design contract
notes.body: The scheduler, window register and metadata queue advance only on their own accepted transfers.

plates.title: FFT and IFFT memory engines
plates.subtitle: Two independent iterative engines each own a work RAM, coefficient ROM and registered butterfly.

nodes.title: Transform work RAM
body: FFT: 56 bits per word. IFFT: 72 bits per word
Port A: load, operand A, output. Port B: operand B

nodes.title: Stage address registers
body: half = span/2, base and j counters
addr A = base+j, addr B = A+half

nodes.title: Held output word

description: The FFT and IFFT are separate engine instances with separate work RAMs. Each holds 256 complex words. FFT components are signed 28 bits and IFFT components are signed 36 bits. Bit-reversed load addresses permit natural-order output.

Eight radix-2 stages contain 128 butterflies each. READ captures operands and twiddles, START launches arithmetic, and WAIT writes the two results. The paired write addresses differ by the current half-span and remain distinct.

The FSM separates memory read phases from write phases. RAM is loaded before compute rather than asynchronously cleared. OUT_SEND holds a captured word across backpressure. Clock count depends on accepted outputs and is distinct from the sample-domain FFT size.

notes.title: Design contract
notes.body: FFT and IFFT reuse a design template, not one physical RAM or butterfly resource.

plates.title: Canonical spectrum and threshold logic
plates.subtitle: Pair averaging, squared magnitude, comparison and complex zero selection preserve real-signal symmetry.

nodes.title: Canonical round register
body: round divide by two, fit signed 28 bits

nodes.title: Complex-bin output selector
body: preserve conjugate relation and frame id

nodes.title: Spectral observation tuple
body: 129 unique bin ids, pre-mask power and decision
valid-only capture feeds TSP1. Complex phase stays on the IFFT path.

description: The canonicalizer stores a full FFT frame and reads conjugate-related pairs. It forms signed 29-bit real sums and imaginary differences before dividing by two with the defined rounding rule. DC and Nyquist retain their real values with imaginary zero.

The negative half negates the already-rounded positive imaginary component. The magnitude path squares the canonical real and imaginary components and adds them in the unsigned 56-bit power domain. The comparator uses frame-owned THR2. Strict less-than drops eligible bins, equality survives and DC is protected.

The spectrum builder selects canonical complex values or exact zero while preserving conjugate symmetry. A separate valid-only observation carries each unique bin, power and decision into spectral capture. TSP1 omits phase and cannot replace the IFFT input.

notes.title: Design contract
notes.body: Canonicalization, thresholding and sparse encoding are separate stages with separate numerical and representation roles.

plates.title: Registered radix-2 butterfly arithmetic
plates.subtitle: Four parallel multipliers feed product registers, complex add/subtract, quantization and butterfly outputs.

nodes.title: Operand register
body: a = ar + j ai, b = br + j bi
w = wr + j wi, twiddle F15

nodes.title: Twiddle quantization register
body: t = tr + j ti, fit to DATA_W

description: The four multiplier symbols represent parallel real products from the same operand registers. They are not a cascade. Each product has DATA_W+17 bits. A widened subtraction and addition form the complex twiddle product before the first rounding point.

Twiddle quantization shifts right by 15 with ties away from zero and saturation. The delayed a operand is added to and subtracted from the quantized t. FFT then rounds a divide-by-two at each stage. IFFT disables that second normalization shift and uses inverse twiddles.

The controller states are B_IDLE, B_PRODUCT_SUM, B_QUANTIZE, B_ADD, B_ROUND and B_OUTPUT. Arithmetic registers use clock enables. B_OUTPUT holds both complex results and saturation status until the engine accepts them.

notes.title: Design contract
notes.body: The two rounding points are explicit hardware operations. Replacing them with one final rounding changes the fixed-point result.

plates.title: Synthesis window and overlap-add storage
plates.subtitle: Frame collection, emit-before-add ordering, ring accumulation and a held output register implement reconstruction.

nodes.title: Frame z buffer
body: two pipeline stages drain before emit

nodes.title: Overlap-add RAM
body: read and write occupy distinct states

nodes.title: Mature sample quantizer
body: emit 128 mature samples BEFORE adding the collected frame
round OLA right shift 15, saturate to signed 12 bits

nodes.title: Y ready/valid register
body: hold data and 64-bit sample index until acceptance
384 tail ticks emit and clear the retained OLA state
SCRUB initializes the OLA ring before collection

description: The synthesis multiplier uses a signed 36-bit IFFT component and a nonnegative 16-bit coefficient extended to signed 17 bits. It produces a 53-bit product. A rounded right shift of 15 fits the result into the signed 36-bit z buffer. This is the first synthesis scaling point.

After a complete frame and its pipeline tail are collected, WOLA emits 128 mature ring entries before adding the frame contributions. Each mature 37-bit value is rounded right by 15 and saturated to 12 bits. The captured slot is cleared. Frame contributions then use address (read pointer +128+offset) modulo384 with a widened 38-bit add and 37-bit saturation.

The z buffer has 256 entries and the OLA ring has 384 entries. Explicit SCRUB initializes OLA storage. Read/capture and add/read/write states respect synchronous RAM latency. The Y register holds data and index under backpressure. Final tail ticks emit and clear retained state without dummy transforms.

notes.title: Design contract
notes.body: Synthesis scales at two different points: product shift 15 and mature OLA shift 15. Combining these into one shift changes fixed-point behavior.

plates.title: TSP1 capture, checksum and packetization
plates.subtitle: Slot ownership, synchronous entry reads, record walking and byte packing turn observations into host records.

nodes.title: Canonical-bin observation
body: frame id, bin id and power

nodes.title: Exporter frame slots
body: frame id, threshold, mode and count
slot remains owned through final byte

nodes.title: Two-pass record walker
body: HASH: header, then payload and padding
EMIT: restart at byte 0, include checksum

nodes.title: Checksum pass and latch
body: authorize EMIT after final hash byte

nodes.title: Byte-to-word packer
body: four byte lanes form a 32-bit word
first three lanes can fill while full

description: The exporter captures unique-bin powers and retain decisions into four frame slots. A 64-bit entry can hold bin: 8 bits plus power: 56 bits. Per-slot metadata contains frame identity, threshold, mode and count. Invalid order or inconsistent frame information triggers the documented discard/recovery behavior.

Dense mode has 903 payload bytes, one padding byte and the 48-byte header, totaling 952 bytes. Sparse mode carries 8K payload bytes and totals 48+8K. At K=129 it is 1,080 bytes and therefore exceeds dense. The checksum includes header bytes 0 through 39 and payload/padding, excluding only bytes 40 through 47.

HASH_FETCH and HASH scan header bytes 0 through 39 followed by payload and padding, skipping checksum bytes 40 through 47. The final hash is latched before EMIT_FETCH and EMIT restart at byte 0 with that checksum included. Synchronous entry reads supply seven dense or eight sparse byte lanes. Final-byte acceptance releases frame ownership. The word packer requires FIFO room on its fourth byte.

notes.title: Design contract
notes.body: Four exporter slots do not mean four admitted frames in the finite profile. Source hop credit limits triggered-but-not-emitted frames to one.

plates.title: I/Q polyphase multiply-accumulate datapath
plates.subtitle: Selected history, coefficient ROM, one multiplier and a feedback accumulator implement four interpolation phases.

nodes.title: I history registers
body: shift on input pair or zero flush

nodes.title: Q history registers
body: shift on input pair or zero flush

nodes.title: Phase and tap registers
body: phase: 2 bits, tap: 5 bits, group: 32 bits
phase advances after crop or accepted output

nodes.title: Quantizer and held sample register
body: MAKE captures sample and clip. HOLD waits for ready

description: The adapter stores 21 centered signed 9-bit samples for I and 21 for Q. The 2-bit phase chooses the history bank. A 5-bit tap index selects one sample and forms coefficient address 4*tap+phase. The ROM contains 81 signed 18-bit values with 16 fractional bits.

One 9 by 18 signed multiplier produces a 27-bit product each MAC clock. Sign extension feeds a 36-bit accumulator. Twenty-one positions are evaluated per phase, including zero coefficients beyond address 80. No per-tap rounding occurs.

The accumulated value uses the phase sign sequence +I, -Q, -I, +Q. Gain selects a final shift from 16 to 13. Half ties round away from zero before signed 12-bit saturation. Output acceptance releases the held result and advances phase. The multiplier is shared across phases, not across FFT butterflies.

notes.title: Design contract
notes.body: One MAC resource evaluates four phases serially. The I/Q history and accumulator registers preserve state during downstream stalls.

plates.title: I/Q adapter controller and finite alignment
plates.subtitle: IDLE, LOAD, MAC, MAKE and HOLD coordinate filtering, startup cropping, output stalls and exact counts.

nodes.title: IDLE / admission
body: start_ready while idle and no error
latch pair count 1 to 96,000 and gain

nodes.title: LOAD / pair ownership
body: accept raw pair when valid AND ready
shift both I and Q histories
after last input, insert signed zero pairs

nodes.title: HOLD / output ownership
body: hold data, index, last and clip

nodes.title: Next phase or group
body: last accepted output: DONE, go IDLE

nodes.title: Finite file-source wrapper
body: rate and RF center remain metadata

description: START admits a finite pair count and gain in IDLE. LOAD shifts I and Q history once for each accepted input pair. After input_count reaches pair_count, LOAD shifts exact centered zeros internally. The flush is not encoded as a fabricated unsigned byte.

MAC evaluates 21 tap positions. MAKE applies the oscillator sign before rounding and saturation. During the first ten groups, phase advance discards startup results. Subsequent results are captured into output registers and owned by HOLD until acceptance.

Four phases per group and ten flush pairs yield exactly 4*N aligned real samples. The file-source wrapper then zero pads the common input transaction. CLEAR aborts even a stalled output, and the enclosing application also clears its consumer so abandoned samples cannot enter another epoch.

notes.title: Design contract
notes.body: Tap advances every MAC clock. Phase advances after a cropped MAKE result or accepted HOLD result.

plates.title: Host register interface and ownership
plates.subtitle: Identity, idle configuration, raw input, output queues and completion counters occupy defined MMIO registers.

nodes.title: HPS MMIO master
body: one active epoch per loaded profile

nodes.title: Input write port
body: TRF1: I in bits 7:0, Q in15:8
TRF1 upper 16 bits must be zero

nodes.title: Host completion check
body: CLEAR before the next admitted START

description: The HPS uses 32-bit aligned MMIO accesses through the lightweight bridge. The bus adapter requires full byte enables, a single burst and exactly one read or write request. FIFO read latency is captured by the DATA state before REPLY. The host verifies profile magic, ABI and source identity first.

THR2 is split across low 32 and high 24 bits. Idle-only configuration prevents an active epoch from changing its input interpretation. TSH2 words are signed 12-bit samples represented as int32. TRF1 words pack two unsigned bytes and reject a nonzero upper half-word.

Status, counters and FIFO pop ports are separate responsibilities. RF conversion exposes its own pair count, gain, clipping and valid-prefix registers. A DONE production bit does not certify that the host has received all results. HPS drains residual data, checks totals and clears the epoch ownership before another start.

notes.title: Design contract
notes.body: All shown addresses are byte offsets. The host admits the loaded profile before interpreting its source-specific register fields.

plates.title: FIFO storage, prefetch and backpressure
plates.subtitle: Queue entries, in-flight reads and output registers own different pieces of the same transaction.

body: read data appears on next clock

nodes.title: Source ready/valid
body: hold data while valid and not ready

body: final packet byte acceptance releases credit
tap observation itself has no ready

body: valid and contents hold under stall
WOLA waits for a free output slot

nodes.title: Spectral partial-word register
body: first three byte lanes may fill while full

nodes.title: HPS feed/drain scheduler
body: queue space permits more input progress

description: The TRF1 input queue has 256 words plus a registered prefetch stage. The prefetch owns a returned synchronous read while the source is not ready. Queue occupancy alone therefore does not describe all in-flight input ownership.

Finite source credit uses accepted source index and emitted-frame count to limit triggered-but-not-emitted frames to one. The valid-only tap is observed without a ready return. Its transport pressure acts on admission of future source hops. The independent Y path holds both value and index until accepted.

The packer owns a partial 32-bit spectral word independently of the output FIFO. Its fourth-byte transfer requires queue room. HPS interleaves bounded input writes and output reads so neither output FIFO is ignored. Host stalls extend epoch duration while accepted ordering and numerical state remain stable.

notes.title: Design contract
notes.body: Data, ids and state advance on accepted transfers. Valid alone does not grant ownership transfer.

plates.title: Finite epoch state and exact tail geometry
plates.subtitle: Source feeding, analysis flushing, WOLA draining, production completion and host reception are distinct phases.

nodes.title: IDLE / configured
body: admit profile, ABI and source digest
START owns a complete finite epoch

nodes.title: Pure WOLA tail
body: 384 ticks bypass input ring and FFT
emit and clear retained OLA state

nodes.title: DONE / pending host drain
body: FIFOs may still hold result words

nodes.title: CLEAR / next epoch setup
body: empty prefetch, queues and packet state

description: The admitted 384,000-sample geometry generates 384,128 analysis tokens, including 128 analysis zeros. At hop 128 this produces 3,001 frames. The first frame includes a conceptual zero left half. The source metadata records which input portion is valid data and which is padding.

After the final analysis frame, 384 WOLA-only ticks drain retained reconstruction history. They do not schedule FFT work. The exact reconstructed output count is 384,512. DONE also requires source completion, core quiescence, emitted spectral records and an empty partial-word packer.

The host may have drained earlier results before DONE, and may still need to drain remaining FIFO words afterward. It checks final totals before CLEAR. CLEAR preserves epoch numbering. Hardware reset restarts it. The 3-billion-cycle watchdog includes transport stalls and is nominally 60 seconds at 50 MHz.

notes.title: Design contract
notes.body: General geometry uses frames=floor((Ns+254)/128), tau_last=128*frames and Ny=tau_last+384. The 128-zero suffix belongs to the 384,000-sample case.

description: CLOCK_50 drives the active application fabric. HPS provides reset assertion and the retained wrapper uses a three-register release chain. Assertion is asynchronous and release shifts high on clock edges. Generated HPS CPU, DDR and Ethernet clocks belong to the platform boundary.

Transform RAM is loaded before compute instead of asynchronously cleared. WOLA storage is explicitly scrubbed. CLEAR cancels queue, prefetch, source, core, exporter and packer ownership together. RF history registers and finite-source counters follow the same abandoned-epoch boundary.

Checks observe accepted transfers, output identities, numerical values and exact counts. TSH2 UVM and formal results retain their module and assumption scope. TRF1 has its own simulation and source-bound board evidence. Source-derived diagrams connect implementation to evidence without claiming a new execution.

notes.title: Design contract
notes.body: Implementation structure and verification scope are recorded separately. Formal CDC/RDC closure and whole-system equivalence are not established by this atlas.
